item.title: Woman who rescued injured crow keeps getting 'thank-you gifts' from birds [video]
item.description:
Source: www.youtube.com

Top Comment:

My late father developed a feeding ritual for a crow that lasted for over a decade and was prompted entirely by the crow’s decision to stand in a particular position, which he would only do if he observed my father in the kitchen. It happened a few times a week on the crow’s own schedule, the same way every time.

There were no gifts but over the years we did witness this crow clearly trying to teach its very dependent growing child how to work the human. Ultimately it never succeeded, and we presume this crow eventually either passed on or moved on. But one of the gaggle of jealous magpies who observed the process did take up the role. Being more timid it didn’t simply stand and wait, but would appear, circle the feeding spot until it got my father’s attention, fly up to one specific branch and wait, but otherwise repeat the process it observed. That went on for a couple of years.

The process itself varied according to what food was thrown out, but the crow slowly developed a particularly clever strategy for carrying off whole stale bread crusts by dragging it to a water bowl, moistening then trimming and diagonally cutting a slot into the bread from one corner almost all the way to the other, such that it could hang either side of the beak in a balanced fashion; the magpie that took over learned this by observation and attempted it from day one.

item.title: JPEG XL vs. AVIF for web use-cases
item.description:
Source: jakearchibald.com

Top Comment:

> libjxl's maximum effort is very slow. It produces files 2–7% smaller than its default for photos, and ~25% smaller for the screenshot and illustration, but takes 9–46 seconds, which is 50–180x as long as its default. jixel gets the same results in a couple of seconds.

libjxl's slow speed at efforts >7 is primarily due to an iterative evaluation-optimization loop of a perceptual error metric called Butteraugli (by tuning quantization weights). This, as well as some other computations in libjxl encoding, happen to be data-parallel and run faster on GPUs than multicore CPUs.

In case anyone is interested, I've been working on a GPU-accelerated libjxl port (supporting CUDA and Metal for now) that makes this much faster, closer to libjxl's normal speeds: https://github.com/yunho-c/gjxl - geared for encoding a large batch images into JPEG XL. It's also faster by around 2.9x at normal effort (7).

item.description:

After the OAI demo, like many others, I tried to use KiCAD through computer-use. This doesn't produce great results.

I have found the best results through a mix of Happy[0], this repo, and computer use to fill in the blanks.

It is _really_ good at the stackup and part config, but creates some absolutely terrible routes. It will snake tiny traces through some SMD pins even though there is plenty of space available outside of the component. When it hits an obstacle, instead of creating 2 45 degree turns, it does 10~30 small ones creating some sort of weird crooked arc.

I have produced a couple of boards for testing this way and they are generally functional.

I have tried KiCadRoutingTools[1] as well which does seem to create routes that make more sense.

Anyone any better experiences with these or similar tools?
